title: The Stone That Speaks
summary: A quarrelsome merchant challenges Birbal to make an ordinary street stone speak in court. Birbal demonstrates that silence itself can speak volumes.
full_text:
A loud, argumentative merchant named Seth Din Dayal was notorious across Agra for dragging his neighbors to court over petty grievances. Frustrated by Birbal's repeated dismissals of his frivolous lawsuits, the merchant decided to humiliate the minister before the Emperor.

Standing in the Diwan-i-Am, Din Dayal placed an ordinary, rough grey stone on the velvet table and declared: 'Raja Birbal claims he can extract the truth from anything! I challenge him: make this stone speak before the court today, or admit that his wisdom is a complete fabrication!'

Akbar frowned at the insolence, but Birbal accepted the challenge with serene grace.

Birbal walked to the table, leaned down, placed his ear against the cold stone, and listened intently for several minutes in complete silence.

The court was hushed. The merchant smirkingly asked: 'Well, Birbal? What does the stone say?'

Birbal straightened up, looked at the merchant with profound solemnity, and said:

'Din Dayal, the stone has spoken into my ear with great clarity. It said: "Tell Emperor Akbar that I am an ancient, peaceful stone that has rested by the roadside for a thousand years. I endure rain, sun, dust, and cartwheels without ever uttering a single complaint or picking a quarrel with a traveler.

'"Yet this merchant before you possesses neither my patience nor my decency! He yells at his neighbors, screams at his wife, and fills the court with noise over every speck of dust! Tell the Emperor that if he wishes for peace in Agra, he should replace this noisy merchant with a quiet stone!"'

The entire court erupted in laughter. Din Dayal turned red with embarrassment and slipped quietly out of the hall. Akbar commended Birbal for turning an absurd insolence into an unforgettable lesson on patience.
moral: Lição de moral: Wit beats power
